subject.title: [Bug] QQ Bot: skill_workshop approval "Allow" button always recorded as rejected

question: When QQ Bot has no configured execApprovals and no explicit non-wildcard allowFrom entry, should a direct C2C callback alone authorize plugin and exec approval decisions?
rationale: Current code intentionally separates message admission from privileged approval authority, while the paired PR makes direct-chat delivery sufficient; repository behavior alone cannot determine that trust policy safely.

options.title: Require verified approval actor
options.body: Preserve fail-closed authorization and accept direct callbacks only when the actor is explicitly authorized or securely bound to the intended approval recipient.

options.title: Trust every direct callback
options.body: Treat all non-group QQ callbacks as approval-authorized, restoring open-DM convenience while weakening the current authority boundary.

options.title: Keep gate, fix UX only
options.body: Continue requiring explicit authorization but avoid presenting actionable buttons to unauthorized actors and return immediate setup guidance.

recommendation.title: Require verified approval actor
recommendation.body: Preserve fail-closed authorization and accept direct callbacks only when the actor is explicitly authorized or securely bound to the intended approval recipient.

likelyOwner.reason: The current boundary originates in their focused QQ fallback-approval hardening work, and this decision directly revisits that contract.
